questions.stem: According to the passage, how many African-Americans had served in the U.S. Senate by 2009, including Obama?
options: Two
Five
Ten
Twenty
questions.evidence: By 2009, only five African-Americans had ever served in the U.S. Senate – and Obama was one of them.
questions.explanation_ko: 2009년까지 미국 상원에서 일한 흑인은 오바마를 포함해 다섯 명뿐이었다고 나와 있습니다.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT true about Obama's education?
options: His father was from Kenya
His parents met at the University of Hawaii
He attended Harvard as an undergraduate
He transferred from Occidental College to Columbia University
questions.evidence: After two years, he transferred to Columbia University in New York.
questions.explanation_ko: 그는 학부 과정에서 컬럼비아 대학교로 편입했다고 나와 있으며, 하버드는 나중에 로스쿨로만 언급됩니다.

questions.stem: What can be inferred from the survey finding that two-thirds of Americans believed racial conflicts could be resolved right after Obama's election?
options: Most Americans believed Obama's election would make racial conflicts worse.
Obama's election was widely seen, even by some who didn't vote for him, as a hopeful sign for racial progress.
No Americans believed racial conflicts could ever be resolved.
Only African-Americans felt any hope after Obama's election.
questions.evidence: A public opinion survey immediately after Election Day found that two-thirds of Americans believed that the country’s racial conflicts could be resolved.
questions.explanation_ko: 당선 직후 실시된 여론조사에서 3분의 2가 인종 갈등이 해결될 수 있다고 믿었다는 내용에서, 그의 당선이 투표하지 않은 사람들에게도 희망의 상징으로 여겨졌음을 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.stem: Why does the author quote Obama's 2004 convention speech saying "There's not a black America and white America... There's a United States of America"?
options: To show the message of unity that helped launch his rise to national prominence
To criticize the Democratic Party
To explain how national conventions work
To describe a policy he passed as president
questions.evidence: He said he was confident the U.S. could overcome its divisions and achieve unity.
questions.explanation_ko: 이 인용문은 그를 전국적으로 주목받게 만든 통합의 메시지를 보여 주기 위한 것입니다.

questions.stem: In the passage, what does "under-represented" mean in "African-Americans have been extremely under-represented in the U.S. government"?
options: present in numbers larger than their share of the population
present in numbers smaller than their share of the population
completely absent
equally represented
questions.evidence: African-Americans have been extremely under-represented in the U.S. government
questions.explanation_ko: under-represented는 인구 비율에 비해 훨씬 적은 수만 대표되고 있다는 뜻입니다.

blanks.expression: put pressure on the city government
blanks.sentence_ko: 그는 공공주택에 사는 사람들이 생활 여건 개선을 위해 시 정부에 압력을 가하도록 도왔다.

blanks.expression: won a seat in the U.S. Senate
blanks.sentence_ko: 그는 압도적인 승리로 미국 상원 의석을 얻었다.
그는 미국이 분열을 극복하고 통합을 이룰 수 있다고 확신한다고 말했다.
많은 미국인에게 오바마의 대통령직은 흑인 노예제를 허용했던 나라에서 중요한 상징이었다.

key_points: Barack Obama, elected in 2008 and re-elected in 2012, became the first African-American U.S. president, at a time when only five African-Americans, including him, had ever served in the U.S. Senate.
Raised partly by his grandparents in Hawaii after his parents separated, Obama studied at Occidental College, Columbia University, and later Harvard Law School.
Before law school, Obama worked as a community organizer in Chicago, helping public housing residents pressure the city government for better conditions.

Obama's message of national unity, highlighted in his notable 2004 Democratic National Convention speech, helped launch his rapid rise from the Illinois state senate to the U.S. presidency within about a decade.
main_idea: The passage traces Barack Obama's path from a childhood divided between Hawaii and Indonesia to becoming the first African-American U.S. president, highlighting his message of national unity.
restate_sentence: For many Americans, Obama’s presidency was an important symbol in a country that permitted black people to be enslaved.
